result:
The 15K peak long run is now 16 km, between the 10K (14 km) and the half marathon (18 km). It's a one-number change in `PEAK_LONG_RUN_KM` in `plan_generator.py`. All the tests pass on temporary copies of the project, after I updated my 15K test to expect 16 km. The real database and the login and signup templates are untouched.

A new runner's long runs on a 10-week plan with four run days now look like this:

| Race | Long runs by week (km) |
|---|---|
| 10K | 2.5, 4.5, 7, 5.5, 9.5, 11.5, **14**, 10.5, 10 |
| 15K | 2.5, 5, 8, 6, 10.5, 13.5, **16**, 12, 11 |
| Half marathon | 2.5, 5.5, 8.5, 6.5, 11.5, 14.5, **17.5**, 13, 12 |

The 15K reaches its full peak in 10 weeks. Because the half-the-week rule still applies, weekly totals for 15K plans rise with the longer long runs. Any 15K plan you've already saved keeps its old runs until you edit it.

The too-short warning bug I flagged last time is still there, so an exactly 10-week 15K plan still gets warned. Just let me know if you want it fixed.
